Merchant

Alexandria, 19 June 1936

Very dear brother,
Your letter is dated yesterday. I receive a receipt on the [B.O.] of the [bank] [illegible]. Amount of [4000] [pounds] [illegible], received by [illegible]. Joseph Khayat has taken care of it [illegible]. My sincere thanks for the Arabic letter from [illegible]. Félix wrote for me to Mister [illegible] in English and told me, in replying to him, that he has already done it. Last night I returned from the telegraph; now it is true. If he is not free for the trip, as he telephones me, I will write to you. Here is the joy of the letter. And the copy of the letter that you sent him concerning the dispatches of the checkbook. I hope you will come tomorrow; we will go. The information at the end of the letter will be given. The dispatches will be by the [B.O.] tomorrow. End of the shipments.
